skills.label: Workspace Foundation
skills.description: Build a portable workspace with useful agent capabilities.
skills.reads: Workspace files, agent instruction files, ignore rules, and the list of available tools/MCPs.
skills.writes: Workspace scaffold files, after showing the proposed content and getting approval.
skills.notes: Auditing a workspace can surface credential-shaped files; the skill reports them instead of reading their contents. Connecting a recommended tool or MCP may lead the user into a separate login, which is their explicit step, not this skill's.

skills.label: Email Digest
skills.description: Turn recent mail into a useful recurring digest.
skills.reads: The contents of a mailbox the user has already connected, over that account's existing access.
skills.writes: The digest and the user's local digest preferences.
skills.notes: Reading mail is a sensitive read of personal correspondence and needs a working mail connection. The skill neither sends mail nor modifies the mailbox; account setup stays with the user.

requires.what: Read access to a mailbox through any mail tool, connector, or CLI the workspace already has.
requires.why: The digest is built from real messages; there is no offline mode and no account setup inside the skill.
requires.verify: Ask the agent to list the senders of yesterday's mail. If it cannot, the connection is missing, not the skill.

requires.what: A file, card, or chat surface where the digest is written.
requires.why: A digest nobody reads on schedule decays into noise; the destination is part of the setup, not an afterthought.
requires.verify: Run one digest and confirm it appears where you actually look.

skills.label: Mail Triage
skills.description: Work a mailbox down in short rounds of real decisions.
skills.reads: The contents of a mailbox the user has already connected, over that account's existing access.
skills.writes: Moves messages between folders inside that mailbox, and a growing local rules file that records what may happen without asking.

requires.what: Mail access that can list, search, read, and move messages between folders or labels. Send permission is not required and should not be granted.
requires.why: Triage is an acting ritual: without move permission it degrades into a digest, which the separate email-digest skill already does better.
requires.verify: Have the agent move one harmless message to a test folder and back before you let it run a round.

requires.what: An ordinary folder inside the mailbox that receives anything the agent believes is junk — not the provider's trash or spam.
requires.why: Nothing in this method is irreversible. Provider trash auto-expires, so a mistake found a month later is unrecoverable.
requires.verify: After the first round, open that folder: everything cleared silently should be sitting there.

requires.what: A writable rules file next to the installed skill, started empty.
requires.why: It is the only thing that licenses acting without asking, and it is how the round gets smarter. A round that leaves it unchanged taught the skill nothing.
requires.verify: Answer one round's cards, let the next round execute them, then confirm the file changed.

requires.what: Any surface that can show a small set of cards and take one line of answer per item.
requires.why: The round is sized to the user's attention, not to the mail count; the cards are where that budget is spent.
requires.verify: Confirm each card carries a stable handle (folder plus message id), otherwise the next round cannot execute your answers.

skills.notes: Acts on personal correspondence: it moves mail, so it needs modify permission on a live account. It never deletes — junk goes to a soft-trash folder inside the same mailbox — and it never sends. Autonomy grows only by the user's approval, and every silent round must show a sample of what it handled.

skills.label: Transcript Intake
skills.description: Turn a meeting recording or transcript into the right durable note.
skills.reads: Meeting recordings and transcripts the user hands over, plus existing notes and the task list, to find the right destination and avoid duplicates.
skills.writes: One extracted note in the workspace's own notes structure, and action items as proposals the user still has to accept.

requires.what: At least one source of meeting transcripts: a local recorder, a notetaker service with an API or connector, or a meeting platform's transcript export.
requires.why: The skill's first step checks sources against each other, because one source alone routinely reports meetings as unrecorded. With a single source that step degrades to a no-op — it still works, it just checks less.
requires.verify: Ask the agent to list the meetings it can see for last week and name the source of each.

requires.what: A notes or knowledge structure the agent can read and append to.
requires.why: Routing to an existing document is the default; without read access the skill can only create new files and the notes fragment.
requires.verify: Ask it to name the document a given topic would be appended to before it writes anything.

requires.what: Somewhere that keeps proposed items separate from committed ones, with already-decided items still visible.
requires.why: Action items from transcripts are proposals, and the skill deduplicates against past decisions before proposing. Without this it either floods the task list or re-raises things already rejected.
requires.verify: Check that a processed transcript left proposals you must accept, not entries already sitting in your task system.

skills.notes: Reads whole conversations, so the source material is sensitive even when the resulting note is not. Connecting a recording source may lead the user into their own login, which is their step. It writes notes and proposals, never commitments toward third parties.

skills.label: Workspace Hygiene
skills.description: Keep an agent workspace tidy and trustworthy.
skills.reads: The whole workspace, including scratch notes, indexes, and instruction files.
skills.writes: Moves, archives, and — only on explicit approval of the exact targets — deletes workspace files.
skills.notes: The only skill here that can remove user files. Every move or deletion is previewed, archiving is preferred over deletion, and deletion requires approval of the exact targets.

skills.label: Superboard Update
skills.description: Check the installed Superboard package and any Superskills copies for updates and install them safely.
skills.reads: The installed Superboard package version, the PyPI release feed, the installed skills' recorded source and version, and this catalogue.
skills.writes: A git snapshot commit before any change, the upgraded package, and — only after approval when local edits collide with an upstream change — a merged skill file.
skills.notes: Reinstalling the package never touches workspace files. The one non-obvious side effect is the safety-net commit: if the workspace was not yet a git repository, the skill initialises one and commits the current state before acting, without asking first. It never writes the board's own configuration, data, or thread files, and never installs a new skill or opens an issue or pull request without an explicit yes in the thread; either of those, if the user agrees, may prompt a git-hosting login the skill does not set up itself.

skills.label: Workspace Learning
skills.description: Turn real corrections into durable rules.
skills.reads: Card threads, completed work, and corrections the user has authorized as learning sources.
skills.writes: Observation notes and, after approval, rule files that shape future runs.
skills.notes: Work history is sensitive content, and promoted rules change how future agents behave, so promotion is always the user's decision.
